text.S1: There once was a married man and woman who wished for a child. At length the woman hoped God was about to grant her desire. These people had a little window at the back of their house from which a splendid garden could be seen, which was full of the most beautiful flowers and herbs. It was surrounded by a high wall, which no one dared to pass, because it belonged to an evil enchantress who had great power and was dreaded by all the world.
text.S2: There was once a man and his wife, who wished to have a child. For a long time, the woman had faith that God would give her, her heart’s desire. This couple had a little window behind their home, where they could see the beauty of the garden, it was full of beautiful flowers and trees. It was protected by a very high wall, such that no one would think to climb over it, because it belonged to an evil enchantress, yet she had power to speak evil words and was disliked by the whole world.
text.T1: Kwali aba upene babili abalefwaisha umwana. Bana Mayo balekabila ukutila Lesa alabapaala no mwana. Aba bantu balikwete akali windo kunuma ya nganda emo balemona ibala iisuuma na Amalia ayalekana-lekana. Yashingulwike na ifibumba ifitali ifyakutiila takwali no wingesha ukupitapo, pantu abene bali ababi umutima, lelo balikwete na maka, elyo bali bapatile Ku caalo conse.
text.T2: Kwali shibantu na namayo abaupene abalekabila umwana. Panshita ntali namayo alicetekele ukutila Lesa akamupela ico akabila. Aba bantu balikwete intolokoso kunuma ya nganda apo balemwena ukuyemba kwe bala, Ilya iswilemo amaluba nemiti iyaemba icine cine. Lyacingililwe necibumba icitali icakuti takwali no wingesha ukupitapo, pantu abene bali ababi umutima, lelo balikwete na maka yakusosa icitu cibi elyo baletinya ne caalo conse.

text.S1: One day the woman, who was standing by the window and looking down into the garden, which was planted with the most beautiful flower, named Rapunzel. It looked so fresh and so green she wanted it and had the greatest desire to eat it. This desire increased everyday, and as she knew that she could not have any, she quietly languished, and looked pale and tired.
text.S2: One day, the woman, who was standing by the window, as she looked on at the garden, where the flower called Rapunzel was planted. It looked beautiful, fresh and green. She really wanted to eat them. Each time the urge got stronger, every day, her desire was so strong that she began to feel ill and tired.
text.T1: Ubushiku bumo bana mayo, abaimanine pe windo elyo baleloleshya mwibaala, umwabyelwe Amaluba ayeshina, rapunzel. Yalemonaka bwino, ayapya elyo na kata hipa-katapa. Balefwaisha ukuyalya. Lyonse, ukukufwaisha kwalekulilakofye cilabushiku, ukukufwaisha kwalilenga batampa no kumfwa ukulwalilila na ukunaka.
text.T2: Bushiku bumo na mayo, uyo aiminine pa ntolokoso elyo aleloleshya mwibala, umwabyelwe amaluba ayeshina, rapunzel. Yalemonaka bwino, mulemfwe mulemfwe ayakatapa-katapa. Alefwaisha ukuyalya. Lyonse, kukufwaisha kwalekulilakofye cilabushiku, ukukufwaisha kwalilenga atampa no kumfwa ukulwalilila na ukunaka.

text.S1: She told the man: "If I can't get some of the Rapunzel flower behind our house to eat, I shall die." And the man thought, “I will bring my wife some of the flower, let it cost what it will”. In the twilight of the evening, he clambered down over the wall into the garden of the evil enchantress, hastily grabbed a handful of Rapunzel’s, and took them back to his wife. The woman made herself a salad of it, and ate it with joy.
text.S2: The woman told her husband: “If I will not eat this flower, Rapunzel that is behind our home, I will die”. Then the man thought, “No matter what, I will bring this flower to my wife”. At dusk, he decided to climb over the high wall and enter the garden of the evil enchantress. Quickly, he collected a handful of Rapunzel, and took them to his wife. This woman made a vegetable salad for herself and ate it with a lot of joy.
text.T1: Abanakashi baebele abalume: " Ine nga nshalye iyi Rapunzel iluuba kunuma ya nganda yesu, nalafwa". Elyo abaume batontonkanya,"Nalaletelako abakashi bandi iluba ilicibe-cibe". Munshita ya mweshi ukutuula, mucuungulo, bapitile pa cibumba nokwingila mwibaala ya ba namayo ababi umutima, mukwangufyanya babulile tu rapunzel utwakwisuusha ukuboko, baletela nabakashi. Bana Mayo bali pekanya no kulya nensansa shonse.
text.T2: Namayo aebele shitata: " Ine nga nshalye ili iluuba Rapunzel kunuma ya nganda yesu, nalafwa". Elyo shitata atontonkanya,"Nalaletelako abakashi bandi iluba ilicibe-cibe". Munshita ya mweshi ukutuula, mucuungulo, bapitile pa cibumba nokwingila mwibaala ya ba namayo ababi umutima, mukwangufyanya babulile tu rapunzel utwakwisuusha ukuboko, elyo atwalila umukashi. Uyu Mayo ali pekenye no kulya nensansa shonse.

text.S1: She, however, liked it so much—so very much, that the next day she longed for it three times as much as before. Her husband must once more descend into the garden. In the gloom of evening, therefore, he let himself down again; but when he had clambered down the wall he was terribly afraid, for he saw the enchantress standing before him.
text.S2: However, she enjoyed it so much- such that, the following day, she wanted some, even ten times more than before. Her husband, once again, entered into the garden of the evil enchantress, yet, this time, as he descended, he found the owner of the garden standing there, waiting for him. He was terribly afraid.
text.T1: Lelo, bali itemwisha nganshi- saana, ubushiku bwakonkelepo balefwaisha nokucilapo. Abalume nakabili baingile mwibaala lya bene, lelo lilya baikila basangile umwine we bala naiminina, bali unfair umwenso icipesha amaano.
text.T2: Lelo, ali tutemenwe nganshi, icakutila ubushiku bwakonkelepo alifwaishe nokucilapo. Abalume nakabili baingile mwibaala lya bene, lelo lilya baikila basangile umwine we bala naiminina, bali umfwa umwenso icipesha amaano.

text.S1: "How dare you," said the enchantress with a very angry look,"you descended into my garden and stole my rapunzels like a thief? You will suffer for it!" "Ah," answered the man."Let mercy take the place of justice, I only made up my mind to do it out of necessity. My wife saw your flowers from the window, and felt such a longing for it she would have died if she had not had some."
text.S2: “How dare you!” said the enchantress looking very angry, “you entered into my garden as a thief and you stole my rapunzel? You will suffer for them!” “Ah,” the man answered, “Have mercy on me, I was not stealing because I am a thief, I only did it out of desperation. My wife saw your rapunzel plant through the window of our home, and she was craving it very much. She even wanted to die if she couldn’t have some”.
text.T1: " Tamwakwata no menso," efyatile bana Mayo ababi umutima, nelinso ilibi,"mwacingila mwibaala landing nga kabolala mwangibila na tu Rapunzel? Mwalatuculila!" "Ah," efyasosele abaume. Mbeleleniko uluse, nshacilaiba pantu ni ne kabolala iyoo. Abakashi bandi bali mona amaluba pe windo yesu, elyo bakwata ukufwaisha, pantu balefwaaisha. Balefwaaya no Ku fwa nga tabalye.
text.T2: " Tamwakwata na menso," efyasosele Mayo ulya uwabuluku, alolesha nelinso lyabukali,"mwacingila mwibaala lyandi nga kabolala mwanjibila na tu Rapunzel? Mwalatuculila!" "Ah," efyayankwile shitata. Mbeleleniko uluse, nshacilaiba pantu teine kabolala iyoo. Abakashi bandi bali mona amaluba pe ntolokoso yesu, elyo bakwata ukufwaisha, pantu balefwaaisha. Balefwaaya no Ku fwa nga tabalye.

text.S1: Then the enchantress allowed her anger to be softened, and said to him,"If the case be as you say, I will allow you to take away with you as much rapunzel as you want, only I make a condition, you must give me the child which your wife will bring into the world. It will be well treated, and I will care for it like a mother." The man, in his terror, consented to everything, and when the woman was brought to bed, the enchantress appeared at once, named the child Rapunzel, and took her away.
text.S2: Then the enchantress’ anger was softened, then she said, “If it is as you have spoken, I will allow you to take as much Rapunzel as you may need, the child that your wife will have, you will give to me, I will take good care of her, as her mother, because of fear, he accepted everything. When the baby was born, the evil enchantress came and gave her the name Rapunzel and took her away.
text.T1: Elyo umwanakashi umubi umutima, baibwelamo panono, elyo Batila,"Nga cili ngefyo mwasosa, nalamisuminisha ukusenda fi rapunzel ifingi, ukuipesha, lelo, umwaana abakashi benu bakakwata mulingile mwampela. Nkamusungafye bwino nga nyiina wakwe, ku mwenso basuminefye fyonse. Ilyo umwana afyelwe, na Mayo no mutima uubi afikile no kumupela ishina Rapunzel nokumu senda.
text.T2: Elyo mayo wabuluku , abweseshemo ubukali, elyo atila,"Nga cili ngefyo mwasosa, nalamisuminisha ukusenda fi rapunzel ifingi, ukuipesha, lelo, umwaana abakashi benu bakakwata mulingile mwampela. Nkamusungafye bwino nga nyiina wakwe, ku mwenso basuminefye fyonse. Ilyo umwana afyelwe, na Mayo no mutima uubi afikile no kumupela ishina Rapunzel nokumu senda.

text.S1: Rapunzel grew into the most beautiful child beneath the sun. The enchantress raised her as her daughter but treated her very cruely. When she was twelve years old, the enchantress locked her in a tower in a forest, which had neither stairs nor doors. At the top was a little window. When the enchantress wanted to climb in, she placed herself under it and cried,"Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair to me." Rapunzel had magnificent long hair, and when she heard the voice of the enchantress she let down her braids, winding them round one of the hooks of the window above, and the enchantress climbed up.
text.S2: Rapunzel grew into the most beautiful girl beneath the sun. The evil enchantress raised her as her own daughter, yet she raised her in a cruel manner. When she turned twelve years old, she locked her up in a tall tower in the bush and it had no entrance, no stairs nor doors. At the top, there was a little window. When the evil enchantress wanted to climb up the tower, she would shout out,”Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your hair”. “Rapunzel had lovely, long hair, when she heard her voice, she would let her hair down and then the evil enchantress climbed up.
text.T1: Rapunzel akulile, nokusanguka akakashaana akasuma nganshi. Abanakashi aba mutima uubi, balimukusisha ngo mwaana wabo, lelo, ukulamu cuusha. Elyo akwenye imyaka ikumi limo na tubili, bailemukomena mu ciyanda icitali mu mpanga, tacakwete na ifibi. Pamulu fye epali akali windo. Elyo, abanakashi ababi umutima balefwaaya ukukweela, balepundila panshi,"Rapunzel, Rapunzel, ikisha umushishi obe panshi". Rapunzel akwete imishishi iitali isuuma, elyo aumfwile ishiwi lyabo, alelekako imishishi shakwe elyo bena bakweela.
text.T2: Rapunzel akulile, nokusanguka akana akayemba nganshi pesamba yakasuba. Mayo ulya umuloshi alikakushishe ngomwana wakwe umukashana, lelo amukushishe buluku-buluku. Elyo afikile imyaka ikumi limo na ibili, bailemukomena mu ciyanda icitali mu mpanga, tacakwete na umwinshi wakupitilapo. Pamulu fye epali intolokoso. Elyo, mayo uwabuluku alefwaaya ukukweela, alapunda panshi,"Rapunzel, Rapunzel, ikisha umushishi obe panshi". Rapunzel akwete imishishi iitali isuuma, elyo aumfwile ishiwi , alelekako imishishi shakwe elyo bena bakweela.

text.S1: After a few years locked in this tower, Rapunzel became miserable. She grew tired and bored of being locked away all these years. It came to pass that the King's son rode through the forest and saw the tower. He heard a song, which was so charming that he stood still and listened. This was Rapunzel, who in her solitude passed her time in letting her sweet voice resound. The King's son wanted to climb up to see her and looked for the door of the tower, but none was to be found. He rode home, but the singing had so deeply touched his heart that every day he went out into the forest alone and listened to it. Once when he was standing behind a tree, he saw the enchantress arrive and he heard how she cried,"Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair".
text.S2: After many years locked up in the tower in the bush, Rapunzel was very miserable. She got tired and bored of being locked up. A prince was passing in the bush, when he saw the tall tower. He heard a lovely song coming from the tower. He stopped and began to listen to the lovely song, this was Rapunzel, passing her time by singing songs. The prince began to look for a way to see the singer in the tower, but there seemed to be no entrance or door in sight. He returned home, but the song had deeply touched him and his heart longed to hear the song again, he returned to the tower everyday alone to listen to it. One day, as he stood hiding, behind a tree, he saw the evil enchantress arrive and he heard her shout, “Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your hair”.
text.T1: Lintu papitile imyaka iyingi balimukomenafye mu ciyanda icitali ca mu mpanga, Rapunzel aliba uwatondobaala. Alitendwa no kunaka ukwikala uwakomwa. Umwana wa mfumu alepita mu mpanga, elyo acimona iciyanda icitali ici. Aumfwile inyimbo iyisuuma nganshi iyale fuuma mu ciyanda icitaali, elyo aiminina alakutika.Limo, lintu a imanine kunuma wacimuti, Rapunzel ewaleimba, aleimba ukuposako inshita. Umwana wa mfumu atampile ukufwaya inshila ya kumwena uleimba, lelo tapalipo inshila. Alibwelela ku ng'anda, lelo ulwimbo lwalimwikata eico, cilabushiku aleeya mu mpanga eka mukumfwa inyimbo. Ubushiku bumo ninshi na imanina kunuma ya cimuti, nafisama. Amwene na maayo wa mutima uubi afiika apuunda,"Rapunzel, Rapunzel ikisha imishishi shobe."
text.T2: Panuma yamyaka iingi iyafumineko, balimukomenefye mu ciyanda icitali ca mu mpanga, Rapunzel aliba uwatondobaala. Alitendwa no kunaka ukwikala uwakomwa. Ubushiku bumo ninshi na imanina kunuma ya cimuti, nafisama. Amwene na maayo wa buluku afiika apuunda,"Rapunzel, Rapunzel ikisha imishishi shobe."

text.S1: Rapunzel let down the braids of her hair, and the enchantress climbed up to her."I will do the same thing," he said, and the next day he went and cried,"Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down the hair." Immediately the hair fell down and the boy climbed up. At first Rapunzel was terribly frightened, by the man whose eyes she had never yet beheld. The King's son told her that in his heart he could have no rest, until he had saved her from the evil enchantress. Rapunzel lost her fear, and realized now she could escape the evil enchantress. And she said,"I will willingly go away with you, but I do not know how to get down. Bring with you a scarf of silk each time that you come here, and I will weave a ladder with it.”
text.S2: Rapunzel let down her hair and the evil enchantress climbed up the tower. He thought to himself, “I will do the same thing”. The following day, he went to the forest and shouted, “Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your hair”. Just then, the hair came falling and he climbed the tower. At the beginning, she was afraid to see a young man she has never met before in her life. The prince told her that in his heart, he will not be at peace till he saves her from this kind of life. Rapunzel was no longer afraid but was happy that she could finally escape the evil enchantress. She said, “I will go with you”, fearlessly but “I don’t know how to get down from here”. “Bring a silk scarf with you each time you come and I will make a ladder out of it, to get down with.”

text.S1: They agreed that he should come to her every evening, for the old woman came by day. The enchantress remarked nothing of this, until once Rapunzel said to her,"Tell me, mother, how it happens that you are so much heavier for me to draw up than the young King's son—he comes this evening." "Ah! you wicked brat," cried the enchantress "What do I hear you say! I thought I had separated you from all evil in the world, and now you have yet deceived me." In her anger she clutched Rapunzel's beautiful braids, wrapped them twice round her left hand, seized a pair of scissors with the right, and snip, snip, they were cut off, and the lovely braids lay on the ground. And she was so pitiless that she took poor Rapunzel into a desert where she had to live in great grief and misery.
text.S2: They agreed that the prince should come and visit in the evening as the evil enchantress would come in the afternoon. The evil enchantress was not aware of this arrangement at all, until one day, Rapunzel said, “Mother, can I ask you a question? Why are you heavier than the prince who comes in the evening?” ”Ah, you evil child”, cried the evil enchantress. “What did I hear you say!” “I thought I had protected you from the evil world, but behind my back you have been deceiving me and seeing a young man?” In her anger, she took Rapunzel’s beautiful locks and twisted it on her left hand twice and cut it and it fell to the ground. She took Rapunzel to a desert, there she lived in great misery and grief.

text.S1: On the same day, however, that she cast out Rapunzel, the enchantress fastened the braids of hair which she had cut off to the hook of the window, and when the King's son came and cried "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair," she let Rapunzel’s hair down. The King's son ascended, but he did not find the dearest Rapunzel above, but the evil enchantress, who gazed at him with wicked and venomous looks."Aha!" she cried mockingly,"You would find my dearest, but the beautiful bird sits no longer singing in the nest; the cat has got it, and Rapunzel is gone; you will never see her again."
text.S2: On the very day, when Rapunzel was taken to the desert by the evil enchantress, she tied her long lock of hair to the window. The prince arrived, he shouted, “Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your hair”, immediately the lock of hair came tumbling down. The prince climbed and was shocked to find the evil enchantress looking at him with utter disgust. She said, ”Aha, you will never see her again, your singing bird is gone, Rapunzel is gone; you will never see her again.”

Attila "Aha", tawakamumonepo na kabili uwiikala aleimba pushi na mu senda Rapunzel naaya; elyo tawaka mumonepo na kabili."

text.S1: The King's son was beside himself with pain, and in his despair he leapt down from the tower. He escaped with his life. He ate nothing, but roots and berries, and did nothing but lament and weep over the loss of his dearest love. Thus he roamed about in misery for some years, and at length came to the desert where Rapunzel lived in wretchedness. He heard a voice, and it seemed so familiar that he wept going towards it, and when he approached, Rapunzel knew him and fell to her knees and wept. The prince led Rapunzel to his kingdom where she was joyfully received, they had a child together and they lived for a long time afterwards, happy and content.
text.S2: The prince, was terribly sad, in his sadness, he jumped from the top of the tower. He managed to escape with his life, he ate nothing at all, he only fed on roots and berries. He roamed around in misery for many years and ended up in the desert where Rapunzel lived in misery. He heard a familiar voice as she sung, he followed the voice, with tears in his eyes, when Rapunzel saw him, she remembered him, she cried, tears of joy. The prince took Rapunzel to his kingdom, where they were so happy to meet her. They lived together and had a child afterwards, happily ever after.
text.T1: Umwana wa mfumu ali umfwa ubulanda nganshi, elyo mu kukalipwa kwabo alitoloka ukufuuma muciyaanda icitali. Alepitana fye mu mpanga ukwabuula ukulya lelo ukupitana fye no kuba cibebebe no kulila ukulufya kwa mutemwikwa wakwe Rapunzel. Elyo apitene imyaka iingi aasuka afika na ku ncende kwali Rapunzel mubucushi. Aumfwile ishiwi yo aishibe, aile aleikonka ne filamba, elyo Rapunzel amumwene amwibukishe, elyo alila ifilamba. Baile bonse ku cipango ca Mfumu eko ba mu pokelele ne nsansa shonse. Baikele pamo inshita iitali mu nsansa ne cibote ica pwililika.
text.T2: Umwana wa mfumu ali umfwile ubulanda nganshi, elyo mu kukalipwa kwakwe alitoloka ukufuuma muciyaanda icitali. Alikwanishe ukupususha umweo wakwe, talile nangu cimo, alelyafye imishila nefinsabwa nsabwa .Alifye necililishi pa kulufya kwa mutemwikwa wakwe Rapunzel. Elyo apitene imyaka iingi aasuka afika na ku ncende kwali Rapunzel mubucushi. Aumfwile ishiwi aishibe, aile aleikonka ne filamba, elyo Rapunzel amumwene amwibukishe, elyo alila ifilamba. Baile bonse ku cipango ca Mfumu eko ba mu pokelele ne nsansa shonse. Baikele pamo inshita iitali mu nsansa ne cibote ica pwililika.
